sources.entry: Turtl - Totally private personal database and note taking app. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 CommonLisp

summary.name: Turtl
summary.one_liner: Turtl is an open source, end-to-end encrypted personal notebook for organizing and syncing bookmarks, passwords, files and notes, with optional sharing and a self-hostable server.
use_cases: keep passwords in an encrypted vault
share private data with family or teammates
run a private notes server at home or work
summary.what_it_does: Turtl lets you organize many kinds of personal data, including bookmarks, passwords, files and shopping lists, and find them later. Data syncs across your devices. The page says it uses high-end cryptography so that only you and people you choose can view your data. You can share selected data with teammates or family without giving up security. The source code is published so it can be read, and you can install your own Turtl server at home or work for more control. The page does not give details on the specific encryption algorithms or client platforms.
notable: Open source with publicly readable code (GPL-3.0, Common Lisp per awesome-selfhosted listing)
Self-hostable Turtl server for users who want control of their data
Encrypted sharing with chosen family or team members
Stores bookmarks, passwords, files and lists in one place
caveats: Premium service is paid; the page says 'Don't want to pay for our premium service?' implying a paid tier exists, with pricing details not given
Supported platforms are not named on the page
Presented as a community project; the page does not state a maintenance or release status
